Berkeley Unified School District 
2026-27 Adopted Budget Report and Multiyear Fiscal 
Projection 
Adoption June 17, 2026 
Local Educational Agencies (LEAs) are required to adopt a budget prior to July 1 of each year in order to 
authorize the expenditure of funds.   The proposed budget is only an initial blueprint for revenues and 
expenditures since the preparation of the adopted budget occurs before the State has enacted its budget, and 
before actual revenues and expenditures are known for the current year. In the event that material revisions 
are necessary, a revised budget will be presented to the Board no less than 45 days after the enacted State 
budget. 
Illustrated below is a summary of the proposed State budget and budget guidelines as provided by the 
county office of education, Business and Administration Steering Committee (BASC), Capitol Advisors, 
School Services of California, Legislative Analyst’s Office, and other professional organizations.   The 
proposed budget report also contains financial summaries, multi-year projections and detailed financial 
state reports relating to the projected financial activity for 2026-27 through 2028-29 specific to the Berkeley 
Unified School District. 
Governor’s Revised State Budget Proposal “May Revision” 
Governor Newsom released his proposed revised state budget on May 14 th   for the upcoming 2026-27 fiscal 
year. 
Proposition 98 Funding 
Revised estimates indicate that Proposition 98 funding for 2026-27 is projected at $127.1 billion, exceeding 
the Governor’s January proposal by roughly $1.6 billion. Across the budget window—comprising the 2024- 
25, 2025-26, and 2026-27 fiscal years—total Proposition 98 funding is estimated to be $6.4 billion higher 
than initially projected in January. It is important to observe that although the Legislative Analyst’s Office 
considers the Governor’s May proposal balanced for 2026-27 and 2027-28, deficits are still anticipated in 
the years following. 
Initially, the Governor’s January Budget for 2026-27 suggested funding the 2025-26 Proposition 98 
minimum guarantee at $5.6 billion below the formula-calculated level. The May Revision maintains this 
approach of appropriating less than the minimum guarantee, though the gap has narrowed to $3.9 billion, 
leading to a proposed $121.2 billion funding level. 
By lowering the appropriation from $125.1 billion to $121.2 billion, the state aims to reduce the risk of 
over-committing funds before final 2025-26 calculations are settled after the fiscal year ends. Unlike a 
formal suspension of Proposition 98, this "settling-up" strategy causes a reduction of approximately $654 
per average daily attendance (ADA). 
Additionally, this process excludes adjustments for cost-of-living or ADA, and repayments are at the 
discretion of the Director of Finance, requiring only a majority legislative vote rather than a two-thirds 
majority. 
Significantly, while the 2025-26 state budget included cash deferrals from June to July 2026, the 2026-27 
May Revision avoids proposing further apportionment deferrals into 2027-28. 
In accordance with Proposition 2, the state must deposit funds into the Proposition 98 reserve when capital 
gains revenues outperform averages. Consequently, the May Revision allocates $8.7 billion in mandatory

A comprehensive Multi-Year analysis can be found in a dedicated section of the budget book. 
Resolution for Budget Adjustments in the Out Years 
The Alameda County Office of Education (ACOE) is requiring districts to submit a resolution for Multi- 
Year Projections that include budget balancing solutions when they adopt the 2026-27 Budget. 
The resolution should include a detailed list and timeline of the budget balancing solutions. The details 
will be compiled using the district’s core values of resource allocations and budget balancing strategies. 
The Multi-Year Projections in the 2026-27 Budget submission identify the need for up to $7.5 million in 
budget adjustments, which are either reductions in General Fund expenditures and/or increases in General 
Fund revenues for years 2027-28 and 2028-29. 
Resolution 26-046 is submitted under separate cover for board approval

COMBINED GENERAL FUND (FUNDS 01-04) 
Revenues 
For the 2026-27 fiscal year, the Berkeley Unified School District's (BUSD) combined General Fund is 
projected to receive   $248.2 million   in revenue.
16:
The primary source of funding is State revenue from the Local Control Funding Formula (LCFF), 
contributing $122.9 million with $116.1 base funding and $6.8 million as supplemental funding. LCFF 
funding accounts for almost 49.5% of the total General Fund. 
The second largest funding source comes from local parcel tax Measures, which provide a total of $68.8 
million, or almost 30% of the total revenue. BUSD is grateful for this vital funding from Berkeley 
taxpayers, which supports small class sizes, enrichment programs, educator salaries, and facilities safety 
and maintenance. The breakdown of these measures is as follows: 
●   BSEP: $46.8 million (18.9%) 
●   BERRA: $12.6 million (5.4%) 
●   Measure H (Maintenance): $9.4 million (3.8%) 
Additionally, $49.7 million (20.0%) is projected from Restricted Federal, State, and Local revenues, 
which must be spent on specific programs. Finally, Other Unrestricted State program revenue totals $4.5 
million, representing 1.9% of the budget. 
Base Grant Funding: 
Grade Span Adjustments: The base grant receives an annual Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) of 
2.87% and an additional LCFF augmentation of 1.44% for 2026-27. The target funding factors per grade 
span are: 
TK-3: $10,698 
Grades 4-6: $10,860 
Grades 7-8: $11,181 
Grades 9-12: $12,958 
Additional Base Allocations: The District also receives $1,113 per student for class size reduction and 
$337 per student for Career Technical Education. 
$4.0 million in Grade Span Adjustment funds. 
$4.3 million in Targeted Instructional Improvement Grant (TIIG) funding. 
$1.1 million for State Transportation. 
$2.0 million add-on for Transitional Kindergarten 
Supplemental Funding: 
The District is projected to receive $6.8 million in Supplemental Funding, which is determined by the 
percentage of pupils eligible for free and reduced-price meals, English Language Learner students, and 
Foster Youth. 
Total LCFF Funding: 
The total LCFF funding, encompassing both the base grant and supplemental funds, is projected to be 
$122.9 million, which translates to $13,755 per ADA.
19:
Restricted State Revenue includes $2.9 million in Expanded Learning Opportunities Grants, $2.1 million 
in After School Education and Safety, $5.8 million in Student Support and Professional Development 
Discretionary Block Grant, $2.3 million in Learning Recovery Block Grants and $1.4 million in 
Proposition 28 Arts and Music Education. There is a budget of $8.2 million for the STRS on Behalf 
Pension Contribution. This amount does not result in additional revenue for the District, because it is 
offset by an equal amount of expense. 
Local Parcel Taxes 
Local parcel taxes, accounting for 27.73% of the combined General Fund revenues, are increasing in 
2026-27. The increases in revenues are due to the 3.0% Cost-of –Living Adjustment (COLA) equal to the 
annual average percentage change in the Bay Area Consumer Price Index - All Urban Consumers, San 
Francisco-Oakland-San Jose area over the prior twelve months, as of December of the prior fiscal year, as 
published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, applies to all of the District’s parcel taxes. 
Parcel tax revenues from BSEP, Measure H, are projected to total $46.8 million. Of the BSEP revenue, 
66% is designated for High Quality Instruction, 27% is designated for Essentials for Excellence and 7% is 
designated for Effective Student Support. 
Parcel tax revenues from Maintenance, Measure H, are projected to total $9.4 million. Measure H of 
2020 replaces Measure H of 2010. These funds are used for school building maintenance and security. 
Parcel tax revenues from BERRA, Measure E, are projected to total $12.6 million. Of the BERRA 
revenue, 5% is designated for Educator Recruitment, Retention and Development Programs, 95% is 
designated for Educator Compensation. 
Other Local Revenues 
Other combined local revenues are projected for 2026-27 total $22.1 million. Unrestricted local revenues 
total $2.3 million and include $0.4 million in leases and rental revenue and $1.9 million in other local 
revenue. Restricted local revenues total $18.9 million and include a $9.9 million apportionment from 
SELPA, $4.3 million in fees and donations for the after-school program, $1.4 million in PTA donations, 
$0.7 million for Mental Health Services, and $2.3 million in other restricted donations. 
COMBINED GENERAL FUND EXPENDITURES 
The Combined General Fund includes revenue and expenditures for unrestricted state and local funds as 
well as restricted state, federal and local funds. Combined General Fund expenditures for 2026-27 is 
projected to be $249.5 million, which includes indirect costs and transfers to other funds and reflects one 
time savings in the Unrestricted General Fund.

EXPENDITURE COMPARATIVE FOR FUND 01 UNRESTRICTED 
GENERAL FUND 
Salaries and Benefits 
The combined General Fund (Funds 01-04) is projected to spend a total of $211.3 million on salaries and 
benefits, accounting for 85% of all combined General Fund expenses. 
For Fund 01 Unrestricted only, the projected cost for salaries and benefits is $113.4 million. This figure 
reflects an increase of $10.7 million from the estimated actuals of 2025-26, resulting from recently 
negotiated salary and benefit increases. Salaries and benefits represent 95.8% of all Unrestricted General 
Fund expenditures. 
Books and Supplies, Services and Operating Expenses 
Unrestricted General Funds are projected to spend on books, supplies, and services and operating 
expenses total $9.3 million. This figure is $4.1 million lower than the estimated actuals of 2025-26. 
Transfers to Other Funds 
The General Fund is transferring $0.55 million to the Self Insurance Fund to meet required reserves for 
Property and Liability Insurance.
22:
Other transfers under the revenue limit funding method include the proportionate share of funding for 
Continuation Education and Special Education based on ADA, and total $0.7 million and $0.8 million 
respectively. The District has elected to continue these transfers under LCFF, and is now a transfer 
within the Unrestricted General Fund, since these programs are now unrestricted. 
Indirect/Direct costs 
The indirect cost percentage is calculated each year by a formula established by the California 
Department of Education. The District’s indirect cost rate for FY 2026-27   is 4.66%. Restricted 
programs and funds are charged indirect costs for support provided by central services. Other Funds 
including the Adult Education, Cafeteria and Child Development Funds are projected to pay $0.6 million 
in indirect costs to the Unrestricted General Fund for support services.   Restricted programs are projected 
to pay $0.8 million which is reflected in the combined General Fund Expenditures as an offset because 
the contribution is coming from restricted programs. Parcel Tax Funds are projected to contribute $2.9 
million in indirect costs to the Unrestricted General Fund for support services. 
CONTRIBUTIONS AND TRANSFERS: 
The Other Financing Sources/Uses category is made up of transfers between the Unrestricted General 
Fund, the Restricted General Fund and other District funds. It also is where revenues are contributed from 
and to other programs or funds. 
Contributions To and From the Unrestricted General Fund 
The Unrestricted General Fund anticipates a $21.4 million contribution from BSEP/Measure E1 parcel 
taxes, which will be used to maintain class size reduction as mandated by the Measure. In turn, the 
General Fund is projected to contribute $34.5 million to the Special Education program and $0.14 million 
to Berkeley Public School Funds. 
Notably, the contribution to Special Education has seen a $1.0 million increase as compared to the 
estimated actuals of 2025-26, based on departmental reports. This increased amount is currently 
considered one-time and will be subject to ongoing evaluation throughout the 2026-27 fiscal year. 
Due to the Local Control Funding Formula (LCFF), the contributions for Continuing Education, Home- 
to-School Transportation, and Special Education Transportation are now internal contributions within the 
Unrestricted General Fund, as these programs are now considered unrestricted. Furthermore, in order to 
qualify for reimbursement in the Transportation program, expenditures must meet or exceed the 
expenditure level of Fiscal Year 2012-13. 
Transfers To and From the Unrestricted General Fund 
The General Fund transfers $.6 million to the Self-Insurance Fund, Fund 67, for the deductible for 
property and liability insurance coverage. This amount is the same as the 25-26 estimated actuals.
